initial_prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational / infographic-diagram.
Create a refined academic architecture diagram, a NEW raster figure, for the M3 image-specific prompt–visual alignment module in an image-captioning system. This is a mechanism figure for a research report, not an infographic poster. Make it exceptionally clean, legible and compact, with thoughtful spatial routing and no tangled connections. Landscape about 16:9, high resolution, white background, subtle pale peach object branch and pale blue relation branch, thin dark gray outlines and arrows, elegant regular serif typography. Flat vector-like scientific illustration. No shadows, gradients, clipart, decorative icons, giant headings, title, footer, legend, training paragraph, watermark, or acronym CSA.

COMPOSITION: Two clearly separated horizontal rows, object above and relation below, with corresponding operations in aligned columns. Use very faint row backgrounds or a thin dashed group boundary. A small row label inside the upper left of each group reads "Object alignment" and "Relation alignment". Main processing blocks use modest corner radii; input/output records have square corners. Labels concise, 1–3 lines each. All arrows straight or orthogonal with right-angle corners, never curved. Route extra connections in short reserved lanes above or below their own row. No arrow through a label or unrelated box, no accidental joins. Put necessary mathematical symbols INSIDE records or attention blocks, not floating all over the page. Large enough font to read at report width.

EXACT SCIENTIFIC CONTENT:
Input original object memory Vo and original relation memory Vr are each 196 × 512. Prompt text is already encoded upstream; M3 does not train or contain the CLIP/UPT/YOLO encoders.
Top object branch:
1. Data record "Original object memory" with Vo and 196 × 512.
2. "ROI pooling" uses original Vo with linked object-region weights.
3. "Concatenate" joins pooled object appearance with object text embedding and box geometry, which arrive from a small separate input record "Object text + geometry". A tiny illustrative example "person" can be inside that data record. This record must feed Concatenate, not the pooling stage.
4. "Slot MLP" converts the concatenated input to object slots.
5. "Masked cross-attention": query Q is original Vo; keys/values K,V are object slots from Slot MLP. Original Vo must have a clearly connected query path; label Q and K,V inside the attention block near their appropriate input ports.
6. A small circle "+" adds the attention result to original Vo via a straight residual bypass. The output data record says "Updated object memory" and Vo′.
Lower relation branch:
1. Its appearance-source record says "Original object memory" with Vo (the SAME original object memory used above, duplicated as a labelled source for clarity).
2. "Pair ROI pooling" separately pools the subject and target features from ORIGINAL Vo. Absolutely NOT from Vr or updated Vo′.
3. "Concatenate" joins these two pooled features with the relation text embedding and pair geometry, supplied by a small separate input record "Relation text + pair geometry". A tiny illustrative example "person riding bicycle" can be inside that record.
4. "Slot MLP" creates relation slots.
5. "Masked cross-attention": Q is ORIGINAL Vr, K,V are relation slots. A compact separate input record "Original relation memory" with Vr must clearly feed the attention query AND its own residual bypass.
6. A small circle "+" adds the relation attention result back to original Vr. Output record "Updated relation memory" and Vr′.

Spatial control: Each row has a compact local control record "ROI links + valid slots" feeding its pooling operation and the mask input of its masked cross-attention. For relation attention the supported region is subject/target union. Prefer thinner dashed orthogonal control arrows to distinguish mask/ROI links from feature-flow arrows. Control wires do not join the visual-memory residual. Place the record so these two routes are short, do not span other row, do not cross the main feature chain. Exact line geometry and boxes must make feature flow distinct from mask control. The design may repeat a small input record rather than drawing a long confusing cross-panel wire.

The Slot MLP is a trainable two-layer MLP with ReLU, and attention is 8-headed; do NOT print detailed layer widths or all dimensions, as the figure must stay concise. No new gates, losses or hallucinated mechanisms. Queries lacking any supported valid slot receive zero update; do not add a gate block to illustrate this. Both output memories go to a downstream decoder outside this figure; don't draw the decoder, caption generation, beam search or reranking.

Aim for the visual refinement of a carefully typeset computer-vision paper architecture figure: meaningful feature records, aligned blocks, a calm hierarchy, minimum necessary words, precise arrow endpoints, and generous but controlled spacing. Prioritize scientific source correctness and readable flow over symmetry. Return only the completed diagram image.
